Home NAS Setup Guide

A NAS (Network Attached Storage) is a storage server connected to your home network. It lets you store files centrally, back up computers, stream movies, and access files remotely.

For a typical home setup, I'd recommend starting with a 2-bay or 4-bay NAS, depending on your storage needs.

Recommended setup
Shop

2-bay NAS — Simple home storage

Good for file backups, photos, documents, and light media streaming. Two drives can be mirrored for protection against one drive failure.

Shop

4-bay NAS — More flexible home server

Better for growing storage needs, multiple users, Docker applications, and larger media libraries.

Basic network configuration
Connect the NAS to your router or network switch using Ethernet. Your computers can access it over Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Setup steps

Install NAS-compatible hard drives.

Connect the NAS to your router with an Ethernet cable.

Open the NAS management interface and install its operating system.

Create a storage pool (RAID 1 or SHR for a typical two-drive setup).

Create shared folders and user accounts.

Enable SMB file sharing for Windows and macOS.

Configure automatic backups and snapshots.

Enable automatic security updates and two-factor authentication.

Important: RAID is not a backup. Keep another copy of important files on a separate device or in the cloud.
